card.name: Last digit of a dose number
card.fires_on: The final digit of a multi-digit number just before a unit such as mg, mg/kg, mL/min or %, in dosing text. Often the last digit of a number like 250, 1000 or 0.45.

modes.label: Final digit before mg
modes.description: Last digit of a whole-number dose right before mg or mg/kg.
modes.example: increase in benign adrenal medullary tumors of male rats exposed to the 25<<0>> mg/kg dose

modes.label: Digit inside a decimal
modes.description: Digit in a decimal or percent value, with the unit following soon after.
modes.example: Do not mix or administer 0.4<<5>>% Sodium Chloride Injection, USP

modes.label: Digit in a range or combination
modes.description: Last digit of a number in a dose range, ratio or combination product strength.

card.writes: It suppresses time and quantity words like years, days, hours and minutes, so the model expects a dose unit such as mg and not a time unit.
card.plain: It marks the end of a dose number, where a unit like mg comes next and not a time word.
